memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When the Lord saw that he had gone over to look, God called to him from within the bush, "Moses! Moses!" And Moses said, "Here I am." "Do not come any closer," God said. "Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground." Then he said, "I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob." At this, Moses hid his face, because he was afraid to look at God." - Exodus 3:4-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God calls him by name, twice — the way you speak to someone you know well. Moses answers, Here I am.

But the very next words draw a line: do not come any closer. Take off your sandals. This ground is holy.

We live in a time that is comfortable with a friendly God and uncomfortable with a holy one. Both are true, and we lose something precious when we forget the second. The God who calls Moses by name is the same God before whom Moses hides his face in fear.

Notice what makes the ground holy. Not the mountain, not the bush. God's presence. Holiness is not in the place; it is in the Person.

Then God identifies Himself — the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. He is saying: I am the God of the promises made centuries ago, and I have not changed.

Jesus later used this exact phrase to prove the resurrection, saying God is not the God of the dead but of the living (Mt 22:32). Those patriarchs were still alive to God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has my familiarity with God quietly drained away my reverence?
2. When God calls, is my honest answer still "Here I am"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy Lord, forgive me for treating You casually. Teach me to come near through Christ with both confidence and reverence. Amen.
